content.title: Design: token override for usersRegenerate
content.description:
Design the programmatic auth override for usersRegenerate. CTO review (mqe1imi4lg) recommends adding an optional { token } param to usersRegenerate that forwards into resolveAuthor, so callers can act on behalf of a named user without setting process.env (not concurrency-safe).

ALTERNATIVE to weigh: relax the self-service check in open auth mode (tracker.ts:1904) — register/revoke already trust the caller in open mode, so making regenerate consistent is arguably correct. This is library-only (no webapp change) but changes security semantics.

Produce a short design decision: chosen approach, exact API shape, affected files, backward-compatibility note. The webapp-developer will review before implementation.

content.content:
## Design Decision: token override for usersRegenerate

### Chosen approach: Option A — add optional `{ token }` param (REJECTED the alternative of relaxing the open-mode self-service check)

### Rationale

Option A fixes the **root cause for all auth modes**, not just open mode. Today the only way for a programmatic caller (e.g. the webapp acting on behalf of an authenticated user) to assert identity is `process.env.AGT_USER_TOKEN` — but the tracker is a process singleton, so two concurrent webapp requests would race on that env var. `resolveAuthor` already supports an explicit `token` (auth.ts:25, 28-38); `usersRegenerate` simply never exposes it. Closing that gap is a one-line, surgical change.

The alternative (skip the self-service check at tracker.ts:1904 when `config.auth.mode === "open"`) was **rejected** because:
1. It only patches open mode — it does nothing for the strict-mode concurrency problem, which is the actual general bug.
2. It weakens security semantics: in open mode any caller could regenerate *anyone's* token. Option A preserves the proof-of-ownership model (you may regenerate a token only if you present it).
3. It introduces a mode-based exception, which is less principled than an explicit identity override that already exists one layer down.

### Exact API shape

```typescript
async usersRegenerate(
  name: string,
  options?: { token?: string },
): Promise<UsersRegenerateResult>
```

The only logic change is forwarding the token into the existing `resolveAuthor` call (tracker.ts:1895):

```typescript
const authResult = resolveAuthor({
  config,
  users,
  requiresWrite: true,
  token: options?.token,
});
```

The self-service check (tracker.ts:1904) stays exactly as-is. With a token supplied, `resolveAuthor` validates it and returns `author = token owner`; the self-service check then confirms owner == target name. With no token, behavior is identical to today (env var / default user).

### Affected files
- `packages/library/src/core/tracker.ts` — method signature (line 1883), `resolveAuthor` call (line 1895), JSDoc.
- No type changes: `UsersRegenerateResult` (types/api.ts:198) is unchanged.
- No CLI changes: `usersRegenerateAction` (cli/commands/users.ts:73) calls without options, identical behavior.

### Backward compatibility
Fully backward compatible. The new param is optional; existing callers passing only `name` get byte-identical behavior. The public signature widens (added optional param), which is a non-breaking widening for consumers of the generated `.d.ts`. The `agt users regenerate <name>` CLI command is unchanged.

### Flag for the webapp (child mqe2743x4q)
In **open mode** there is no incoming user token, so the webapp must obtain the target user's current token to pass into the override. The library intentionally does not expose token lookups (`usersList` strips tokens). The webapp, as the trusted boundary in open mode, should read the token from `users.json` directly (it already has filesystem access via the tracker dir). This is a webapp-side decision and out of scope for the library change. In strict mode the webapp simply forwards the authenticated user's token from the request — no lookup needed.

### Net change size: ~3 lines in tracker.ts + JSDoc.
